name: Treaty with the Delawares, etc., 1809 (Treaty of Fort Wayne)
aka: Treaty with the Delawares, Potawatomi, Miami and Eel River, 1809
nations: Wea (now part of the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: Permanent annuities for the cession: $500 each to the Delawares, Miami and Potawatomi, and $250 to the Eel River (Article 3), with $5,200 in goods delivered (Article 6).
The Treaty of Greenville's terms on annuity payment and the Indians' right to hunt on ceded land would apply (Article 4).
The Wea's consent was needed to complete the title, with goods and a permanent annuity of at least $300 to be settled on them (Article 5).
The Miami acknowledged the Delawares' equal right to the White River country, which neither could sell without the other's consent (Article 2).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the Miami and Eel River were paid $18,728, under a cent an acre, for their interests in Royce Areas 71 and 72 ceded by this treaty (about 2.09 million acres in Indiana). It valued their part of Area 71 at $1,933,300 and Area 72 (the Twelve-mile Strip) at $850,000 on 16 January 1810, held both considerations unconscionable, and awarded $1,919,535.20 and $845,125.

breaches.what: For the Wea's 549,081 acres in the western part of Area 71, worth $686,400, the Wea were paid $7,500; the Commission held this unconscionable and awarded $678,900 to the Peoria Tribe on behalf of the Wea.

landTaken: Area 71 ceded by this treaty and the Wea convention of 26 October 1809 contained 2,095,688 acres; Area 72, the Twelve-mile Strip, 547,630 acres (Docket 253 findings, 1969). The Commission also found settlers on Area 72 as early as 1803 and 1804, before it was ceded.
compensation: Annuities and goods valued by the Commission at $18,728 for the Miami and Eel River interests in Areas 71 and 72, and $7,500 for the Wea interest in Area 71. Awards of $1,919,535.20 and $845,125 (Miami and Eel River) and $678,900 (Wea) in 1969.
today: The Delaware and Potawatomi interests in this cession were not part of these dockets.

nationVoice.nation: Myaamia (Miami Tribe of Oklahoma), through the Myaamia Center's community blog
nationVoice.summary: A Myaamia Center history says Mihšihkinaahkwa (Little Turtle) was removed from civil leadership after the Treaty of Fort Wayne because most Myaamia held that the ceded lands belonged to the Miami Nation alone and that the Delaware and Potawatomi he brought into the talks should not benefit from their sale.

openQuestions: Whether Delaware or Potawatomi claims for this cession were heard by the Commission was not traced.
A Miami Tribe of Oklahoma statement on this treaty was not found; the Myaamia Center's Aacimotaatiiyankwi blog may have one.
Royce Area 73 (Article 9, the cession for the Kickapoo) is recorded under kappler-111 and kappler-112.
